text: If the person is fully alert and able to swallow, I would give cyproheptadine early, since it blocks serotonin receptors. So far, the evidence for it has only been case reports, and a recent review found them too weak to show that it works. I wouldn't wait to see whether it does before doing the other steps.
section: Suspected Serotonin Syndrome (SS): Do this immediately when serotonin toxicity is reasonably suspected
reader: someone sitting with a friend who shows signs of serotonin toxicity after a serotonergic combination (an MAOI brew, MDMA, an antidepressant, tramadol ...), working down the guide's numbered steps and deciding whether to give cyproheptadine and how much to lean on it

sentences.s: If the person is fully alert and able to swallow, I would give cyproheptadine early, since it blocks serotonin receptors.
sentences.payoff: they give cyproheptadine early if the person is fully alert and can swallow, and know why: it blocks the serotonin that's in excess
sentences.follows: step 1 stopped the serotonergic substances; this is the next thing to do

sentences.s: So far, the evidence for it has only been case reports, and a recent review found them too weak to show that it works.
sentences.payoff: they know how far to lean on it: the evidence is case reports, which a recent review found too weak to show it works
sentences.follows: the limit that decides how much the step's remedy can be counted on, said first (lesson 19a)
sentences.link: So far, the evidence for it

sentences.s: I wouldn't wait to see whether it does before doing the other steps.
sentences.payoff: they go on with the other steps (calling help, cooling) without waiting for it to work
sentences.follows: what the weak evidence means for what they do now

checked.point: the case series the step links (PubMed 9696181, Graudins et al. 1998)
checked.found: five patients given 4-8 mg by mouth, three with no signs left within 2 h, the other two after a repeat dose; "it is unknown whether cyproheptadine modifies patient outcome"; "an adjunct to supportive care"
checked.still_needed: yes: they know the evidence for it is case reports, which is how much they can lean on it; the series itself goes (the three reads: no use to the reader, and it reads as proof)

checked.point: the systematic review the step links (PubMed 39791184, King & Rotella 2025)
checked.found: twelve reports from 2003 on (eleven case reports, one series), every one very low evidence and at high risk of bias; "a lack of evidence to support the efficacy of cyproheptadine"
checked.still_needed: yes: they know the reports are too weak to show it works, so they do the other steps without waiting

placement: Suspected Serotonin Syndrome's immediate steps, step 2, after stopping all serotonergic substances and before calling emergency help and cooling

question_text.Q1: Why am I reading this sentence, and do I know it before I have to work through it? (the point first, in each sentence and each paragraph; a study after the question it answers; a term explained where it is first used, never in a sentence after it)
question_text.Q2: What is each instruction for, said in the reader's terms, and is it something the helper does ("have someone go with them"), not a rule stated as a fact ("someone goes with them")?
question_text.Q3: Which thing exactly? (pools of water, not water; any substance, not anything)
question_text.Q4: What does each word act on, or mean here? (adjunct remedy; known-genuine) Is every term a high-school graduate wouldn't know (enterocytes, BPC-157) explained once, where it is first used, and common ones (a vitamin) left alone? Is each mechanism explained by what it does in the reader's experience (dopamine "for motivation (by showing us what is important to pay attention to)"; DeltaFosB "preventing that learning from really clicking"), not by where it sits or what it looks like ("a chemical blanket", "the slower one underneath")? (E375)
question_text.Q5: Why does each sentence follow from the one before? (every but, so, because and this has what it turns on)
question_text.Q6: Is this the order the reader is thinking in, and does each idea sit next to what it continues?
question_text.Q7: Does each fact help this reader now, in their case (the same kind of thing they face, not just the same topic)?
question_text.Q8: Does each item belong in the group it is put in?
